title: Sex Differences in the Detection of Parkinson's Disease from Speech
abstract: arXiv:2611.24741v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disease in the world, and 70\% to 75\% of PD patients suffer from speech disorders at some stage. Since PD affects men more frequently than women, previous publications tend to rely on unbalanced datasets that potentially introduce sex biases into trained models. This study investigates sex differences in PD detection from speech using deep learning and traditional machine learning approaches. We evaluated speech-based PD detection using embeddings from three pre-trained speech models, combined with handcrafted acoustic features and different classifiers. Sex-specific experiments were conducted on balanced subsets of four sustained phonation datasets, controlling for sex, disease status, and, where possible, age. translated_title: 从语音检测帕金森病中的性别差异
translated_abstract: 帕金森病（PD）是世界上第二常见的神经退行性疾病，70%至75%的PD患者在某一阶段会出现言语障碍。由于PD在男性中的发病率高于女性，以往的研究往往依赖于不平衡的数据集，这可能为训练的模型引入性别偏见。本研究使用深度学习和传统机器学习方法，探究了基于语音的帕金森病检测中的性别差异。我们使用三个预训练语音模型的嵌入，结合手工设计的声学特征和不同的分类器，评估了基于语音的PD检测效果。在四个持续发声数据集的性别平衡子集上进行了性别特异性实验，对性别、疾病状态进行了控制，并在可能的情况下控制了年龄。所有录音均在持续发声任务中采集。结果表明，女性说话者的分类准确率高于男性说话者。
tldr: 本研究通过在性别平衡的数据集上结合预训练语音模型嵌入与手工声学特征，首次系统揭示了基于语音的帕金森病检测存在性别差异，女性说话者比男性说话者能被更准确地分类。
en_tdlr: This study systematically reveals sex differences in speech-based Parkinson's disease detection by combining pre-trained speech model embeddings with handcrafted acoustic features on sex-balanced datasets, showing that female speakers are classified more accurately than male speakers.
